title: Gonzalo Fernández de Córdoba (the Great Captain) to Lorenzo Suárez de Figueroa, 17 Aug 1500, in the Cifra general de los Reyes Católicos: BnF Espagnol 318 no. 92, f. 116r-v (catalogue item 9)

documents.route: Gonzalo Fernández de Córdoba -> Lorenzo Suárez de Figueroa (Venice); copy for Almazán

plaintext.source: Partial decipherment by a later hand between the lines of f. 116r (eight words, ct92_glosses.txt)

transcription.source: Gallica full images (full/f116r.jpg, full/f116v.jpg); f116_reading.md (36 + 11 lines)
transcription.notes: Both pages transcribed line by line on 21 Sept 2026 against Galende's p. 167 sign alphabet; no token count kept (prose reading with the transcription per line).

system.summary: The Cifra general de los Reyes Católicos (Galende Díaz 1994, app. 1, from BRAH 9/15 ff. 7-9): a homophonic alphabet of invented signs (up to five forms a vowel, a duplicate sign for LL) interleaved with a one-part nomenclator of three-letter CVC groups (initials v, x, y, z, b, c) and 21 personal signs.
system.sibling_key: Cifra general de los RRCC (Galende Díaz 1994, app. 1), transcribed here as keys/cifra_general.txt (683 code groups + 21 personal signs)
system.notes: Split on 14 Oct 2026 under the one-key rule: this entry was the whole volume (five letters in at least four ciphers) and now keeps no. 92 only. The others have their own entries: federico1497 (no. 5, Escrivà's cipher), esp318no95 (no. 95, Lasry's alphabet), esp318no93 (nos. 93 and 94, key unknown). The segmentation pipeline, the scans and the shared literature stay in this folder.

prior_solution.where: Key printed by Galende Díaz 1994; Tomokiyo assigned the letter to it (cryptiana spanish.htm) and has an unpublished partial reading of the opening (commented out in the page source); the later interlinear gloss on f. 116r

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.
tools: decode.py (Cifra general applied to a transcription)

solution.what: Mapped the five ciphered letters in the volume from the manifest and notice (catalogue listed four); no. 92 was the one the catalogue had missed.
No. 92 matched to the Cifra general (Galende Díaz 1994) against eight interlinear glosses, no misses; key transcribed (683 groups).
No. 92 specimen line decoded: 'y tiempo, por estar en tanto'.

No. 92 ff. 116r-116v transcribed line by line (36 + 11 lines) by eye from 1:1 line strips of the 4155-px scans, against Galende's p. 167 sign alphabet; A5 (⊃#), E5 (q over k), LL (crossed T) and the con- abbreviation identified as frequent signs.

No. 92 read in part (f116_reading.md): the Great Captain's terms for joining Venice against the Turk in 1500 — ports in Italy (Brindisi, Otranto in Apulia held by Venice) for sick, wounded and supplies; about three quarters of words; 11 codes contradict Galende's printed values in context (zie, zap, bog …).

No. 92 second pass online: Tomokiyo's commented-out partial reading (cryptiana spanish.htm) fixes zap=zag, bac=vac, xie=cargo; Sanuto Diarii III corroborates the port/victuals demand; RAH 9/15 not digitised; no printed clear copy found (CODOIN, Zurita, BRAH Noticias, archive.org).

No. 92 recto ll. 8-11 re-read with Sanuto's terms as cribs (cruciata, jubileo, precedence, paid victuals): none present; the re-read settled zie = parescer (zie+RIA 'pareceria tener'), vog = acatamiento, zer read as zec = mas, and ll. 8-11 now read in sense.

Split from the former whole-volume target esp318 under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): no. 92 (Cifra general) stays here; no. 5 (Escrivà's cipher, printed by Parisi) became federico1497, no. 95 (Lasry's alphabet) esp318no95, nos. 93-94 (key unknown) esp318no93. Steps that concerned only the other letters moved with them; the earlier steps are kept as recorded.

outcome.method_basis: No. 92 was deciphered with the Cifra general printed by Galende Díaz (1994), which Tomokiyo had assigned to the letter; the project proved the assignment against eight interlinear glosses on f. 116r.
outcome.fraction_read_source: NOTES.md and f116_reading.md: 'about three quarters of the words' of no. 92 (an estimate by line from the prose reading; no token-level unread marks)

gaps.item: five code groups (bog x3, zeb, zems, xob, bue)
gaps.detail: They contradict Galende's printed values wherever they stand; his 1994 plates visibly misprint others, so the manuscript BRAH 9/15 ff. 7-9 (not digitised) would settle them.

gaps.item: about ten stretches of letter signs (grade I)
gaps.detail: Mostly where the q-shaped N and the reversed-9 S cannot be told apart at Gallica's 4155-px resolution; each placed stretch was settled by the word.

outcome.notes: Both pages transcribed and about three quarters of the words deciphered (21 Sept 2026). The other ciphered letters of Espagnol 318 are separate entries (federico1497, esp318no95, esp318no93).
